name: Cat Ba National Park
kicker: Forested limestone peaks in the island's heart
summary: Limestone forest in the island's heart: climb Ngự Lâm peak in a morning for the widest view of Cát Bà. The gate is open 07:00–17:00. The golden-headed langur lives only here, in small numbers. Pick the park when you want a walk on land between bay days.
getThere: Road from the town into the island interior
bestMonths: Year round; winter suits the walks
heroCaption: Tree roots over limestone on the forest floor
body: Trails leave the park center and climb through limestone forest, where tree roots spread over the rocks, toward Kim Giao and Ngự Lâm peaks. From the top you look across rows of green karst ridges toward the bay.

Cát Bà became a national park in 1986 and joined the Ha Long Bay–Cat Ba Archipelago World Heritage property in 2023. It is the only home of the golden-headed langur, a critically endangered primate whose small population lives in scattered groups.
Longer routes cross the island. The trek past Ao Ếch, a forest pool, reaches Việt Hải village on the Lan Ha side. Trung Trang cave is on the same route ticket as the two peaks.

figures.caption: The view from Ngự Lâm peak over the park's forested karst
figures.alt: Green limestone ridges under cloud seen from Ngu Lam peak

gettingThere: The park lies in the island interior, reached by road from Cát Bà town. Go by motorbike or taxi, and start early so the climb fits inside the gate hours.

legs.heading: From Cat Ba town
legs.body: By motorbike or taxi into the island interior to the park center.

legs.heading: The long walk
legs.body: From the park past Ao Ếch to Việt Hải village, 8–12 km depending on the route.

admissionNote: From 1 January 2026, adult / child from age 6: park entry 160,000 / 80,000 đồng. Under 6 is free. Route tickets: Kim Giao peak, Ngự Lâm peak, and Trung Trang cave 120,000 / 60,000; Ninh Tiếp field and Tiền Đức cave 80,000 / 40,000; Phù Long, the mangrove, and Thiên Long cave 80,000 / 40,000.
